title: Infineon and ZuriQ Deepen Partnership to Advance Scalable Quantum Chips
source_used: The Quantum Insider (full text of the joint press release read)
key_facts: Infineon Technologies AG and ZuriQ AG, a Swiss quantum computing company spun out of ETH Zurich, announced an expanded collaboration to advance scalable quantum computing hardware.
The partnership combines ZuriQ's trapped-ion architecture with Infineon's semiconductor manufacturing, advanced packaging and integrated photonics.
Earlier joint work trapped a 3x3 array of nine individually controlled ions, which the companies say is the largest two-dimensional array of its kind to date.
The next step is to scale the technology to significantly larger qubit counts; no timeline, figures or prices are given for it.
ZuriQ uses a two-dimensional Penning micro-trap design that moves ions across the chip with electric and magnetic fields.
quote_evidence: The next step in the partnership is to scale the technology to significantly larger qubit counts.
With our expertise in semiconductor manufacturing, integration and advanced packaging, we are enabling the next generation of trapped-ion quantum processing units.
why_it_matters_hint: A company partnership announcement for larger trapped-ion chips; no new results or dates are given.
